query_text: What allowed humans to safely drink water before purification was invented?

message.content:
Based on my search, humans relied on several natural and simple methods to safely drink water before modern purification was invented:

## Natural Water Sources

**Clean groundwater sources** were the primary safe drinking water sources. Early humans and civilizations relied heavily on:
- **Springs and fountains** - The Zulu people, for example, used springs and fountains exclusively for drinking water, believing the soil naturally purified this water. Rivers were used only for washing and bathing because animals contaminated them.
- **Wells** - These were among humanity's earliest water "purification" facilities. Archaeological evidence shows wells in ancient China (around 6000 years ago at Hemudu), Egypt, Mesopotamia, and the Indus Valley. Wells provided more stable and cleaner access to groundwater.

## Early Water Treatment Methods (Pre-Modern Purification)

People developed several simple treatment methods thousands of years ago:

| Method | Time Period | Description |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| **Boiling** | ~4000 B.C. | Ancient Sanskrit and Greek writings recommended boiling water |
| **Sunlight exposure** | ~4000 B.C. | Exposing water to sunlight |
| **Charcoal filtering** | ~4000 B.C. | Filtering water through charcoal |
| **Straining** | ~4000 B.C. | Removing visible particles |
| **Settling/Storage** | Ancient times | Letting water sit so particles settled |
| **Alum treatment** | ~1500 B.C. (Egyptians) | Using alum to cause suspended particles to settle out |

## Key Factors That Made Water "Safe"

1. **Natural filtration through soil and rock** - Groundwater from springs and wells was naturally filtered as it percolated through earth layers
2. **Avoiding contaminated surface water** - Many cultures instinctively avoided river water for drinking
3. **Physical distance from settlements** - Water sources were often kept away from human and animal waste
4. **Aesthetic judgment** - People used taste, clarity, and smell as crude indicators of water quality (though this was imperfect)

## Important Caveat

People did not truly understand waterborne disease until much later. The germ theory of disease wasn't demonstrated until the late 1800s by Louis Pasteur, and John Snow didn't prove cholera was waterborne until 1855. Before this, many water treatment methods focused on improving taste and appearance rather than removing invisible pathogens. Many people likely suffered from waterborne illnesses without understanding the cause.

The first city-wide disinfected water system wasn't built until 1804 in Paisley, Scotland, and routine disinfection of community drinking water didn't begin in the U.S. until 1908 in Jersey City, New Jersey.

Sources:
1. https://www.roundmountainwsdco.gov/the-history-of-drinking-water
2. https://wisa.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/WISA2008-P061.pdf
3. http://iwh.cssn.cn/xscg/zmsyzts/202104/t20210419_5327544.shtml
4. https://archive.epa.gov/water/archive/web/pdf/2001_11_15_consumer_hist.pdf
5. https://repository.ias.ac.in/27268/1/27268.pdf
6. https://engineering.rowan.edu/_docs/civilenvironmental/environmental-engineering-lecture.pdf
